differentiation.occupancy_preservation: This objective contains no explicit uniform-occupancy penalty: it preserves occupancy only insofar as the directed behavior pairs support diverse assignments. Reject it if code usage becomes more concentrated than control or downstream recall declines.

vs_r8.why: Uses directed soft item-to-code assignment cross-entropy, not NCE over hard L1 code transitions; it directly differentiates through codebook rows.
Does not train an L1 next-item semantic prediction head; the behavior target acts on assignments to the existing codebook.
Does not match successor-profile distributions with JS divergence; it trains a directed conditional assignment objective.
Does not solve an entropic OT quantization or assignment problem; its normalized per-item soft assignments are directly optimized against behavior-paired targets.
Does not distill a teacher across three levels; it applies the same directed objective to the selected codebook level.
Does not preserve graph diffusion distances; it uses observed directed source-target behavior pairs.
Uses Euclidean soft code assignments rather than hyperbolic gyro-translation.
Does not form hyperbolic Frechet successor barycentres; target behavior is represented by its soft code assignment.
Does not impose a hyperbolic radial hierarchy or branching structure.
Does not optimize a hyperbolic graph-code Gromov-Wasserstein objective.
Unlike the untouched host control, this adds a behavior-conditioned directed loss with a differentiable path into codebook rows.

differentiation.vs_reference_arm: Unlike the previously measured encoder-only auxiliary arms, this objective differentiates through codebook-dependent soft assignments. The host overwrites encoder gradients but leaves codebook gradients untouched, so the codebook path can alter learned representations and, after re-export, hard L1/L2/L3 SIDs. Hard SID assignment itself is discrete and receives no direct gradient; changes are indirect through updated encoder/codebook parameters.

equation: For each valid directed pair (b), define q_k(x_b; E) = exp(-||x_b - e_k||^2 / tau) / sum_j exp(-||x_b - e_j||^2 / tau). The loss is L = -sum_b m_b sum_k q_k(t_b; E) log(q_k(s_b; E) + epsilon) / (sum_b m_b + epsilon).
expected_failure_modes: Zero or non-finite codebook gradients indicate a broken assignment or loss path; codebook rows and exported SIDs may then remain identical to control.
Collapsed code usage, increased code-frequency concentration, or degraded downstream recall indicate that behavior supervision has over-organized the codebook.
A symmetric loss implementation would fail the source-target exchange invariant and would no longer implement the directed mechanism.
A detached assignment or stop-gradient through the codebook assignment probabilities would prevent the claimed codebook organization.
A loss that does not become zero when all pairs are masked indicates incorrect mask handling or normalization.

forbidden_substitutions.reason: Symmetrizing the directed cross-entropy changes the mechanism and can erase the required source-target exchange sensitivity.
Detaching codebook assignment probabilities blocks the claimed codebook gradient and repeats the encoder-only failure under the host gradient overwrite.
Blocking gradients to the codebook prevents this mechanism from moving the representation organization that the host leaves trainable.

hypotheses: Behavior-directed targets will shape codebook geometry through gradients on the codebook rows, so the host's encoder-gradient overwrite will not erase the entire mechanism.

The asymmetric source-to-target assignment objective will preserve behavior-relevant directed structure better than an ER-only objective; select it only if matched downstream recall@10 improves over r8_control without violating the existing ER gate.

Use a fixed auxiliary weight of 0.01 for the initial matched comparison; retain the mechanism only if the independent checks pass, exported SIDs differ from control, and the cold-run downstream criterion is met.

revision.reason: proposed from the ledger's supported findings, not from a fixed lever list
revision.supersedes: the two families the ledger measured in issue #105

symbols.E: Rows e_k of the codebook level being regularized.
symbols.L: Mean directed assignment cross-entropy over valid source-target behavior pairs.
symbols.b: Index of a source-target pair in the batch.
symbols.epsilon: Positive numerical stabilizer for the logarithm and valid-pair denominator.
symbols.k: Codebook row index, from 1 to C.
symbols.m_b: Binary validity mask for pair b.
symbols.q_k(x; E): Soft assignment probability of representation x to codebook row k.
symbols.s_b: Source item representation for pair b.
symbols.t_b: Behavior-associated target item representation for pair b.

tests.statement: On the supplied synthetic case with at least one valid pair, the loss is finite.
Permuting codebook rows leaves the scalar loss unchanged within tolerance.
Exchanging source and target changes the scalar loss by more than tolerance on the supplied non-degenerate synthetic case.
Masking every pair yields exactly zero loss, up to the declared tolerance.
With a valid non-degenerate case, gradients with respect to source, target, and codebook are finite and nonzero.

On the host mini case, confirm the auxiliary term changes the codebook gradient after host assembly; do not rely on an encoder-only gradient surviving the host overwrite. In a matched cold run, compare exported SIDs and downstream recall@10 with r8_control; require the existing ER gate and improved recall@10 to retain the mechanism.

title: Behavior-directed code-assignment cross-entropy
